text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: I will fire ministers who oppose government policy.
- New York court convicts three for airline bomb plot.
- United States: Iraq pulling back from Irbil.
- Yeltsin to undergo heart surgery.
- Classified Israeli army documents delivered to "Jerusalem Post".
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu threatens to sack ministers who "don't fall into line with the government's basic platform".
- Iranian sources: Since Netanyahu election, Israel has moderated its tone on Iran.
- Israeli-Palestinian steering committee for peace talks to create subcommittee to discuss troop redeloyment in West Bank town of Hebron.
- Neither President Ezer Weizman nor Netanyahu will speak at October 24 memorial ceremony for slain prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, at request of Rabin's family.
- Army deputy brigade commander in north sacked for sending task force across border with Lebanon without coordination with superior officers.
- Police recommend bringing to trial former soccer players Eli Cohen and brothers Shlomo and Arye Shirazi.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu: If I must, I will sack ministers.
- Yedioth Ahronoth poll: 82 percent of Israelis say Netanyahu's meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was "a correct step".
- Israeli who was kidnapped in Columbia freed after 18 month ordeal.
- Abusive husband released from prison, drives home, stabs his wife.
- Scores of illegal casinos for children and teens operating in Israel.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu: Ministers who don't fall into line with the government will be sacked.
- Maariv poll: Overwhelming majority of the Israeli public supports Netanyahu-Arafat meeting.
- Foreign Minister David Levy to London "Times" - "Israel warned Iraqi President Saddam Hussein: If Scud missiles fall in our territory, Baghdad will be destroyed".

- Rabin's widow Leah to President Weizman, after Weizman failed to mention Rabin in opening address to parliament last June: "Now I understand why you came to the hospital (after the November shooting) - you wanted to be sure Yitzhak was dead".
GLOBES
- Committee to issue recommendations: End of stock market crisis: not in the short-term. There should be no promise of "safety net" for provident funds. No tax to be levied on short-term savings.
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor: We will break linkages between wage levels of various sectors.
